prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1492; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the claimant describing a collision at an intersection while making a left turn. The claimant is not represented by an attorney and has been asked to provide photos and a written statement.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was active at the time of the reported collision. Nothing in the policy file suggests any damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 3: Reviewed photos supplied by the claimant. They show the rear quarter panel and bumper damage consistent with the described impact, and a few older scratches are visible that may predate this loss.

Entry 4: Police report obtained. It confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene and references a left-turn collision, though no independent witnesses were identified.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant by phone. The account of how the collision happened matched the first notice of loss in every detail, including the sequence of the turn and the point of impact.

Entry 6: Received medical records reporting a wrist fracture. The injury type and force implied by the collision are a good fit for this kind of impact. No prior injury to the same area is known from the claimant's history or available records.

Entry 7: Treatment has continued for somewhat longer than is typical for this type of fracture. Follow-up notes are being requested to confirm the reasons for the extended care schedule.

Entry 8: Repair estimate reviewed against the photos and the reported impact. The vehicle damage pattern lines up with the described collision, and the adjuster has noted the older scratches separately for the estimate.

Entry 9: Claimant gave a second recorded statement that repeated the same account of the collision. File remains open pending the follow-up treatment notes and final review of the photos.
